summary: A paired phone can approve, not only deny, the approval cards an agent's Switchboard MCP pull request writes open: create_pull_request, reply_to_conversation, resolve_conversation, comment_on_line, draft_review and rerun_check. Rationale: a device with the chat scope can already send the agent full-access turns, which run commands on the desktop; approving a post whose text the card shows is a smaller power. Backend: RESPOND_TO_REQUEST lets a chat-scoped device approve a hostWrite card (was admin), logs which device session approved, and refuses a review approved without a verdict or with one the card did not offer (hostWriteApprovalProblem), leaving the card open so the user can pick again; every later guard (re-checks after the card, plan mode, budget, link rule, expiry, cancel) is unchanged. The Reviews human write channels (PullRequestWriteChannels) stay admin-scoped. The push says 'Needs approval: <write> on <PR>' instead of 'Approve at the desktop', and the plain-text detail no longer ends with 'Answer this on the desktop' (both phone cards say what applies themselves) Wire: the phone reuses the RESPOND_TO_REQUEST 4th argument (parseHostWriteResponse) and sends only resolve (reply) or verdict (review); it never edits. Compatibility: the backend adds the ready capability agent_host_write_phone_approval_v1; a phone offers Approve on a hostWrite card only when the backend advertises it, so a newer phone on an older desktop keeps the Deny-only card, and an older Expo phone on a newer desktop keeps its own Deny-only card. An older native Android app already showed Approve on these cards (the backend refused it); on a newer backend that Approve now posts the agent's draft as shown, except a review, which is refused for want of a verdict. Content: RESPOND_TO_REQUEST keeps only resolve and verdict (approvalChoiceOnly) from a device without the admin scope, so a phone's approval posts exactly the draft its card showed; the desktop keeps editing. Both phones render hostWritePreview (the whole title, description, reply, summary and every review comment with its path:line, from the hostWrite payload), never the capped hostWriteDetail; a long draft starts collapsed and nothing approves until it is opened, and a payload missing what the approval would post is Deny only ('Approve this on the desktop'). Expo: the card shows the write's title, host / PR / location, the full preview, an action-named primary button, 'Post and resolve' for a reply, and for draft_review one button per offered verdict with none primary, a verdict that cannot go as drafted disabled with the reason. Android: the same in its approval row (HostWriteCards.kt ports shared/host-write-phone.ts). Proof of what was shown: a phone approval (no admin scope) must carry shown, the hostWriteShownDigest of the draft it rendered in full (FNV-1a 64 over the preview sections, ported to Android as HostWriteCards.shownDigest); the broker recomputes it and refuses a missing or different one with 'Update the Switchboard app to approve this here, or approve it on the desktop.' An already shipped native Android APK, which showed the capped detail, therefore can no longer approve (it could not before this PR either); deny needs no digest, and the desktop needs none. The digest also binds the request id and the card's target (HostWriteCard.target: repository and PR number, null for a create, plus host and the create's branches), so a digest for one card never approves another card or the same text on another PR.

automated: npm run typecheck and npm test -- --maxWorkers=2 (root vitest): agent-approvals (a chat-scope phone approves a host write as drafted; a review needs a verdict and refuses one the card did not offer, keeping the card open; a device without the scope is refused and may still deny), switchboard-mcp-integration (through ProviderRegistry and the real MCP bridge: a remote device with no scopes is refused, a phone with the chat scope approves a reply as drafted and it posts the agent's text with the marker, against a fake Reviews service), mcp-pr-tools (a review approved without a verdict or with an unknown one, and an author's Approve, are refused at the card and nothing posts), device-auth (every PullRequestWriteChannels channel stays admin-only while RESPOND_TO_REQUEST is open to a phone), agent-host-writes (phoneHostWriteButtons labels, primaries, responses and the verdict problem; hostWriteApprovalProblem; the push text), mobile-approval-actions (Approve only with the capability, Deny only for the legacy cached flag, the capability is in BACKEND_CAPABILITIES), mobile-chat-store (the hostWrite card rides on the approval row).

npm test --prefix apps/mobile (jest, feed-items): the ordinary card offers Approve and Deny; a hostWrite card on a backend without the capability, or a legacy desktopOnly row, offers Deny only; a reply card names the write and context, offers Post reply and Post and resolve, says Edit on the desktop, and a tap sends { resolve: true }; a review offers Comment, Request changes and Approve and a tap sends the verdict; an author's review offers Comment only.

./gradlew --offline testDebugUnitTest (apps/android): HostWriteCardsTest (decode, title, context, buttons, review verdicts and problems, response JSON), ThreadInteractionPolicyTest (approvalActions by capability, the response on the UI action), ThreadSessionCoordinatorTest (the response reaches the remote; backendTakesPhoneApproval from the capability), SwitchboardRemoteClientTest (the 4th RESPOND_TO_REQUEST argument), CachedThreadStateMapperTest (a cached hostWrite card is restored). ./gradlew lintDebug compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin passed.

Round 2 (CodeRabbit): switchboard-mcp-integration (a chat-scoped phone that sends replacement text posts the agent's draft; the desktop's edit is posted), mobile-approval-actions (hostWritePreview holds every word uncapped under its path:line, a create's whole description, null when the payload lacks what would post; approvalChoiceOnly keeps only resolve and verdict; a card without a full preview is Deny only). Expo jest feed-items: a 40-line reply and a four-comment review render every word, their buttons are disabled until Show the full draft, and a review payload without its comments offers Deny only with Approve this on the desktop. Android HostWriteCardsTest (preview sections, long flag, null on a missing reply, comments, create or an unknown action) and ThreadInteractionPolicyTest (a long reply and a long review carry every word and are approvable only once opened; a review without its comments is DenyOnly).

Round 3: agent-approvals (a phone approval without the digest, or with another draft's, is refused with the update message and the card stays open for a deny; the desktop needs none), switchboard-mcp-integration (through the registry an old-style phone approval is refused and nothing posts, then one with the digest posts the draft), mobile-approval-actions (the digest of one pinned card, unchanged by fields the preview leaves out, null without a preview; every host-write button's response carries it), Expo feed-items (the tapped button sends resolve or verdict with the digest), Android HostWriteCardsTest (the same pinned card gives the same digest; the response JSON carries shown) and ThreadInteractionPolicyTest (the button response carries the digest).

Round 4: mobile-approval-actions pins two cross-implementation vectors (a reply on acme/app #612, request sbmcp_42; a Bitbucket create feat/x -> main, request sbmcp_43), computed independently in Python, and asserts a different request id, PR number, repository, host or target branch changes the digest while agentLabel, maxChars and prLabel do not; agent-approvals refuses card A's digest, and the same text's digest under card B's id but card A's target, for card B; HostWriteCardsTest asserts the same two vectors and the mismatch cases in Kotlin. CodeRabbit outside-diff fix: hostWriteApprovalProblem now runs reviewFromResponse before the card settles, so a review the host would refuse (GitHub request changes without a summary, a Comment with nothing in it) is refused with the card left open (agent-approvals).
notExercised: No phone or emulator was run: the Expo card was checked through jest renders only and the Android card through unit tests of its policy; the Compose ApprovalRow layout (FlowRow of buttons, the collapsed and scrolling preview) was compiled but not looked at.
No real GitHub or Bitbucket write was made; every host call in the tests ran against fakes.

Release lanes (docs/releasing.md): the Expo app is the iOS client and its change is JS only (no native module, permission or app.json change, so the fingerprint is unchanged), so it ships over mobile-ota.yml (EAS update, --platform ios). Native Android needs a signed APK: bump versionName / versionCode and dispatch mobile-release.yml. Neither release was run.
